BREAKING: US consumers aged 40-49 now account for 26.8% of new consumer bankruptcies, their highest proportion since Q3 2015 and the largest among all age groups.

At the same time, the 50-59 group represents 23.1%, bringing the combined proportion of Americans aged 40-59 to 49.9%, the largest since Q1 2017.

To put this into perspective, this figure peaked at 54.3% in Q4 2011, following the 2008 Financial Crisis.

Furthermore, those aged 70+ now make up 21.5% of all new consumer bankruptcies, their largest proportion since Q2 2017.

Meanwhile, Americans aged 18-29 now account for only 5.9% of new bankruptcies, their lowest percentage since Q2 2014.

Older Americans are falling behind on their debt.

Global oil demand is declining sharply amid rising prices:

The IEA has cut its forecast for 2026 global oil demand by -940,000 barrels per day, now expecting consumption to fall -2.5 million barrels per day, the largest annual decline since the 2020 pandemic.

This compares with a -1.6 million barrel per day drop expected in August and just a -100,000 barrel per day expected decline in April.

To put this into perspective, in January, the IEA saw oil consumption rising by over +700,000 barrels per day in 2026.

The downgrade comes as the Iran War disrupts oil supplies and forces consumers to adjust to tighter availability, with the biggest impact expected on diesel and other middle distillates such as jet fuel and heating oil.

The negative impact on oil demand this year is expected to be comparable in size to the 4 largest demand shocks over the last 60 years.

Oil demand is collapsing as prices surge.

Greg Brockman on the next year at OpenAI and what he spends his time thinking about:

"The business is a huge area that we're not done yet with really up-leveling every part of execution. But I also think we are moving into a new phase of AI development."

"We call this the AGI era. And I think that that is something that you can debate. Is it this model, previous model, next model? It doesn't matter."

"The point is that we are in a new phase where safety, security, alignment, really thinking about these things, not just at deployment time, but all the way back at development time, evaluation."

"It's objective. This is critical. It must happen. This is core to our mission."

"A lot of what I spend my time thinking about is making sure, do we have all the right processes? Are we talking about the right things? Do we have plans that really, at an operational level, at a practical level, lead us to... the kinds of safety guarantees that we view as core to our mission?"

"The theme of OpenAI, certainly for the past five years, has been deeper co-design, deeper intertwining across these functions that are maybe on the surface very disparate. All the way from go to market to long-term research to chip design."

"The areas that I will focus on will be dictated by the areas that most need that intertwining."

@gdb @eriktorenberg

Greg Brockman on the defenders' window that closes when frontier AI capabilities become distributed:

"Hugging Face shows... what future capabilities will be like when they are broadly diffused and in the hands of threat actors. And that will happen."

"In the case of Hugging Face, you saw both an AI that was able to hack out of a secure environment and hack into a company's production environment."

"This capability broadly diffused is something that will really empower threat actors in new ways. Defenders need to use this time before that technology's broadly available to secure themselves. The nice thing about it is it's dual-use."

"If you can find vulnerabilities, if you're an attacker, you can use it for no good, but if you're a defender, you can patch. If you're a defender, you control the battleground. You control the setup of your systems."

"Our belief right now is that there's this window... You need to move, use these frontier capabilities that you will have differential access to... and you can use that to move yourself up so that as the frontier capabilities get better, you get pulled along too."

@gdb @eriktorenberg @bhorowitz

The US housing market is officially a buyer's market:

There were an estimated +57.9% more home sellers than buyers in August, the biggest gap on record.

This is up sharply from +52.1% the month before, which was the 2nd-strongest buyer's market on record.

This comes as the number of active sellers surged +3.9% MoM, or +57,958, to 1,534,918, the most since early 2020,marking the largest monthly increase on record.

At the same time, there were ~972,300 active homebuyers, the 2nd-lowest reading on record.

This brings the gap between active sellers and homebuyers to a massive 562,618.

As a result, 36 of the 49 major US metros are now buyer's markets, led by Nashville, where sellers outnumber buyers by +139%, followed by Miami at +138%, and Houston at +131%.

Historically low affordability is causing buyers to quit.

Greg Brockman on the only kind of problem he'll work on:

"You cannot affect the outcome. You can only affect the inputs... You don't win the Super Bowl by saying, 'I wanna win the Super Bowl.' You win it by blocking and tackling. That's what we have done for this whole year."

"Throughout OpenAI, I have always focused on whatever is the most important problem that I think I can move the needle on that just isn't gonna happen without me."

"For the past two years, it's been the data centers, the infrastructure, the machine learning engineering... This year, it's really been about the business."

"We've figured out how to get the research really humming. We figured out how to get the infrastructure really humming. But how do we really bring this technology to the world?"

"A lot of my style is that I like to lead from the trenches, and so I get very deep in the weeds on what the thing is and really try to keep asking a lot of questions... really trying to up-level execution, sometimes in small ways and sometimes large."

The biggest update to DefiLlama's dashboard editor ever. Building and customizing dashboards is now more intuitive and faster.

Some highlights from the new version our llamas cooked:

1) Quick add: cmd+k in edit mode, type "uniswap fees" or "aave vs compound revenue" and the card is added
2) Parameters: dashboard level chain / protocol switch in the top bar, all connected cards update; build one dashboard and use it for multiple protocols or chains
3) Sections and tabs: group cards into collapsible sections or split the dashboard into tabs
4) Custom data: upload CSVs and chart them
ui polish kit for the whole dashboards area
5) Hover tooltips sync between charts, add annotations, and more

Reminder that you can create one custom dashboard for free: https://t.co/YV1cNxlGWC

Stocks tend to get the midterm blues, and 2026 is a midterm year.

Since 1986, the S&P 500 has averaged a 3.5% loss from July 1 to a month before the midterms. Some runs were brutal: down 18% in 2002, down 13% in 1990 and 1998.

The flip side: the 12 months after a midterm are historically the strongest of the entire 4-year cycle. Weakness now has usually been the setup for that.

India's inflation 'problem' is a grocery and fuel bill, and the calls for the RBI to hike into it are already piling up.

August CPI hit 4.82%, driven by food at 5.95% and oil above $108. Core is still just 4.2%, and the print sits inside the 2-6% target band. This is a supply shock, not overheating.

A rate hike does not grow rice or pump crude. Hiking into food and oil just kneecaps a 7.8% economy. India's own governor said as much. The hike chorus is not listening.

tweets.text:
Core inflation (ex-energy) has been above 2% for too long. 

When cyclical employment growth was contracting, there was a plausible reason to keep waiting, and core inflation did cool from 6.5% to 2.5%. 

Now cyclical employment growth is increasing, which means the bias for core inflation is higher and that risks core inflation staying above target for even longer.

Raising rates comes with constraints and trade-offs. Housing investment has been contracting since 2022 and will continue to contract. Debt levels are extremely high, so positive real rates won't last too long.

But with cyclical employment growth rising and the 3M10Y at +100bps, tightening isn't a near-term policy mistake. 

Will they get in 4+ hikes? That depends on how much housing bites and how much business equipment investment offsets it.

What you wouldn't expect, if governments weren't captured by the same pharma companies, is any interest in prevention. Healthcare has climbed to around a fifth of what Western governments spend, and the line only goes up.
No one seems to care about preventing disease, only treating it once you're already sick.

The pandemic ghouls

Just look at the so-called spokespersons for health they paraded out during COVID, in Australia, Belgium, Canada, the United States, wherever you looked. 
Don't go out in the sun. Social distance. Take a dangerous experimental vaccine. Natural immunity doesn't work.
No health treatments exist other than Remdesivir and the shot. Stay home until your symptoms are so bad you have to go to the hospital.
De-register doctors and nurses for pursuing empirically better outcomes.
 When the CDC's own data by the second quarter of 2020 showed overwhelmingly that people with metabolic disease and other pre-existing conditions were the only ones at risk

The dependence is the product

Imagine a society that incentivised health instead of treating sickness. Less doomerism, more optimism, healthier bodies and minds, more people running their own lives and fewer looking for handouts.
What they are turning us into instead is patients for life, dependent on the pill, the script, and the system. The dependence is the product. And AI has given pharma an infinite profit stream now.

AI to the Rescue

Ironically, AI is the way we dig ourselves out of this, and now there are products coming to market that can empower people to become their own doctor with AIs built on clean, non-pharmaceutical bullshit marketing data 

This isn't an endorsement. It's just one example I've seen recently that I am keen to try out. Long may this trend of self-empowerment continue because we know the governments will not look out for us

Bitcoin and crypto will suck capital from every asset class. That's the trade.

This market is roughly $3T today. Over the next 5-10 years I think it gets to $10-20T, and that capital has to come from somewhere.

But a trade against everything is hard to track. So I distil it down to the two peers people frame Bitcoin against most: gold and technology stocks. Watching when momentum inflects from bearish to bullish against them after a long bear market is the simplest way to see the rotation happening in real time.

On a weekly chart you can abstract away a lot of the day-to-day and even week-to-week volatility. The shift is underway. It won't be smooth, but the next several years will be crypto's most meaningful structural market.
